map.每日饮水量建议 使用指南: Daily Water Intake Recommendation User Guide
map.根据体重、运动时长与环境温度，估算每日建议饮水量，并结合活动强度给出分次饮水建议: Based on weight, exercise duration and ambient temperature, estimate the recommended daily water intake and give a schedule of drinking occasions by activity intensity, as a scientific reference for maintaining fluid balance in fitness and high-temperature work.
map.基础量(ml) = 体重(kg) × 系数；运动补充 = ⌊运动分钟 ÷ 30⌋: Base (ml) = weight (kg) x coefficient; exercise supplement = floor(exercise minutes / 30) x 250 ml; total = base + exercise supplement + environment adjustment (hot +500 / dry +300 / cold -200 ml); cups = total / 250
map.根据体重、运动量、环境温度估算每日基础饮水与运动补充量，避免脱水或过量饮水。: Estimate daily base water intake and exercise supplementation from weight, exercise amount and ambient temperature to avoid dehydration or over-drinking.
map.健身/高温作业人群按运动时长追加补水，量化「运动时该喝多少」。: For fitness and high-temperature workers, add fluid according to exercise duration to quantify 'how much to drink while exercising'.
map.比对不同体重与活动水平下的饮水基准，制定个性化喝水计划（如分 8 杯水）。: Compare water intake benchmarks for different weights and activity levels to build a personal drinking plan (for example, splitting it into 8 glasses).
map.：输入：体重 65 kg、运动 30 分钟、基础系数 30 ml/kg。\n计算:
: Input: weight 65 kg, exercise 30 minutes, base coefficient 30 ml/kg.
Calculation: base requirement = 65 x 30 = 1950 ml; exercise supplement about 250 ml (estimated for 30 minutes of moderate-to-high intensity); total about 2200 ml/day.
At the common 250 ml per cup this is about 8.8 cups.
Conclusion: this adult is advised to drink about 2200 ml per day (about 8-9 cups), and on exercise days or in hot environments another 300-700 ml should be added on top of this.

For most adults 2000-2500 ml/day is enough; patients with heart or kidney disease must follow medical advice on fluid restriction and should not simply 'drink more water'.
map.咖啡、茶算入每日饮水量吗？: Do coffee and tea count toward daily water intake?
map.算，但有前提。咖啡、茶、汤、果蔬都含水分可计入总量，但咖啡因有轻度利尿作用，建议: Yes, with conditions. Coffee, tea, soup, fruits and vegetables all contain water and count toward the total, but caffeine has a mild diuretic effect, so plain water should be the main source with other drinks as supplements; alcohol is instead diuretic and cannot replace water intake.
